The journey

From power plants to a pan-African research lab

Sixteen years that took him from commissioning generators in Dar es Salaam to leading research and innovation at one of Africa's leading science institutions.

  1. 1

    From the field

    Thomas began as an electro-mechanical engineer, sizing and commissioning power generators across Tanzania, including a 4 MW synchronised plant at Golden Jubilee Towers and backup power for new CRDB Bank branches. He then earned an M.Tech cum laude and a PhD in mechanical engineering at Tshwane University of Technology in South Africa.

  2. 2

    Building a research home

    Since joining NM-AIST in February 2016 he has founded the Clean Energy Technologies Research Group and the Sustainable Energy Lab, risen to Associate Professor in 2023, and turned field problems such as rotting harvests and spoiled vaccines into six patented technologies.

  3. 3

    The work ahead

    As Director of Research and Innovation, he is leading NM-AIST into new partnerships such as the EU's LEAP-ENERGY PLUS and SUNRISE programmes, and helping Tanzania design innovation hubs, incubation programmes and research funds that will carry science into industry.

Research and innovation

Technologies built in his lab

Patented designs and flagship research programmes, funded by partners on four continents.

View all projects

EU ARISE

Solar–biogas hybrid dryer

Dries crops by sun during the day and by biogas at night. Patent TZ/P/2024/000032.

PASET RSIF

Solar-powered vaccine cooler

Off-grid cooling research for remote settings. Patent TZ/P/2024/00096; storage conditions depend on the application.

US National Academies

Solar dryer with thermal storage

Rock-bed heat storage keeps drying going after sunset. Patent TZ/P/2023/000088.

PASET RSIF

Solar-assisted heat pump dryer

Energy-efficient drying for fruit, maize and groundnuts. Patent TZ/P/2023/000093.

EPFL and UM6P

Biofuels from non-food plants

Biodiesel and bio-jet fuel from croton, water hyacinth and farm waste, with natural antioxidants.

EU Erasmus+

Smart solar microgrids

Demand management, load forecasting and power quality for mini-grids in Arusha, Zanzibar and Lake Victoria.

UNIDO

Waste to energy

Rice husk gasification and briquettes, and biogas from abattoir effluent, for agro-industries.

Fondation Botnar

Clean energy skills for youth

A programme targeting 100+ marginalised young people, including youth with disabilities, for clean energy training.

Creating impact

Three roles, one mission

Clean, affordable energy for African communities, and the people and policies to deliver it.

Researcher and innovator

Turning African energy problems into patented solutions

Recognised as NM-AIST's Best Innovator of the Year and a Fulbright African Senior Research Scholar, he leads research that moves from the lab bench to farms and clinics.

  • Solar and hybrid drying technologies
  • Biofuels and natural antioxidants
  • Heat pumps and natural refrigerants
  • Microgrids and smart energy systems

Educator and mentor

Training the engineers who will power the continent

He has taught at university level since 2013 in Tanzania and South Africa, coordinates the MSc and PhD programmes in Sustainable Energy Science and Engineering, and examines for institutions in Tanzania, Kenya and South Africa.

  • Graduate supervision in sustainable energy research
  • Renewable and solar energy courses
  • External examiner in Tanzania, Kenya and South Africa
  • STEM mentoring for Arusha schools

Policy advisor and speaker

Shaping how Tanzania funds and uses innovation

Ministries, the National Planning Commission, UNIDO, the African Development Bank and IUCN call on him for clean energy and innovation policy, and he speaks at forums from Cape Town to Milan.

  • National innovation and incubation task forces
  • Africa Energy Market Place 2024 for AfDB
  • Keynote, World Science Forum 2022
  • Visiting professor, Politecnico di Milano
